correctness.rationale: For any ring in scope, Soc(R)=m^2 is a one-dimensional residue-field space. Products in m yield a nondegenerate symmetric form on m/m^2. Each nonzero quotient vector has q lifts, and each nonzero socle element is universal. Correcting for self-vertices produces two consecutive outer degree values, with multiplicity q times the count of nonzero isotropic vectors. Orthogonality similarities give graph isomorphisms; the degree histogram separates distinct even-dimensional form types and recovers q,d. Every form type is realized by an explicitly constructed short local algebra. Standard finite-field symmetric-bilinear classification proves the form cases. The included checker enumerates all zero-product edges in ten instances, q=2,3,4, d=3,4, including both even-dimensional types.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact classification of ordinary zero-divisor graphs of short finite Gorenstein local rings across all residue-field characteristics and all embedding dimensions >=3. It settles whether and how those graphs detect the field order, dimension and intrinsic radical multiplication geometry, exposes a characteristic-two alternating/nonalternating split, and supplies all degree multiplicities and an exact edge formula. It is not an isolated small-parameter count. Main limits are this short-socle family and dependence on a foundational prior bilinear criterion.
